rv.q: The play, under the lively direction of Guardian critic Brian Logan, is a slippery to-and-fro of strategy, speculation and cunning.

The chess device starts to feel strained – frustratingly, from my seat, I couldn’t make out if the match actually made sense – and the dialogue lacks authenticity, always sounding as if it were written by an adult.

cn.t: Katy Nixon's two-hander earns praise for its unexpected tension and insightful exploration of adolescent dynamics, with critics highlighting strong performances and the play's clever inversion of power between two contrasting classmates.
